{{Short description|American professor}}
'''Lee R. Kump''' is a professor of geosciences at Pennsylvania State University and a fellow of the [[American Geophysical Union]]. He is currently the Dean of the College of Earth and Mineral Sciences at Pennsylvania State University. His research interests include biogeochemical cycles, environmental biogeochemistry, and atmosphere/ocean evolution. With [[James Kasting]], he is the co-author of the popular textbook ''The Earth System''.<ref>[https://www.amazon.com/The-Earth-System-3rd-Edition/dp/0321597796 The Earth System]</ref>

Kump highlights the relationship between the [[climate crisis]] and mass extinction in Earth's history: “The rate at which we’re injecting CO<sub>2</sub> into the atmosphere today, according to our best estimates, is 10 times faster than it was during the [[End-Permian extinction|End-Permian]] [...] And rates matter. So today we’re creating a very difficult environment for life to adapt, and we’re imposing that change maybe 10 times faster than the worst events in earth’s history.”<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/07/29/opinion/sunday/when-life-on-earth-was-nearly-extinguished.html|title=Opinion &#124; When Life on Earth Was Nearly Extinguished|first=Peter|last=Brannen|work=The New York Times |date=July 29, 2017|via=NYTimes.com}}</ref>
